dedupe_keys.name: eia short term energy outlook steo monthly 18 month forecasts of us and world energy markets

description: The Short-Term Energy Outlook is the monthly forecast of the U.S. Energy Information Administration, covering an 18-month horizon through the next calendar year. It is released on the first Tuesday after the first Thursday of each month; the edition read was released on 9 September 2026 with the forecast completed on 3 September, and the next release was due on 6 October 2026. Tables and figures cover global oil markets, petroleum products, natural gas, electricity, coal and renewables, and the economy, weather and carbon dioxide, including US energy market summaries, energy prices, international crude oil and liquid fuels supply, consumption and inventories, OPEC and non-OPEC supply, and a winter heating fuels table. A data browser, real prices viewer and global energy security supplements are provided. Coverage is the United States with world oil markets. Tables are free as PDF and Excel; as US government works they are in the public domain and EIA asks for acknowledgement. Caveats: these are forecasts revised each month, not observations. Simulation uses are near-term demand, price and inventory scenarios for fuel supply stress tests and winter readiness studies. Related records: data-eia-annual-energy-outlook gives long-term projections.
